questions.question: The process in which people grow plants and look after animals is called
questions.explanation: Agriculture is the science and art of cultivating plants and raising livestock.

questions.question: The first animal to be tamed was
questions.explanation: The dog was the first animal to be domesticated by humans, having descended from an extinct species of wolf.

questions.question: The first two crops which was domesticated is
questions.explanation: Wheat and barley were among the first crops to be domesticated in the Fertile Crescent region around 10,000 to 11,000 years ago.

questions.question: The first two animals which were domesticated was
questions.explanation: Dogs were the earliest animals to be domesticated, followed closely by sheep and goats during the early Neolithic period.

questions.question: About how many years ago did the domestication of animals and plants start?
questions.explanation: The domestication of plants and animals began roughly 12,000 years ago (around 10,000 BCE) with the beginning of the Neolithic Revolution.

questions.question: Mehrgarh is present in day
questions.explanation: Mehrgarh is a significant Neolithic site located in the Balochistan province of present-day Pakistan, lying on the Kacchi Plain near the Bolan Pass.

questions.question: Koldihwa is in present day
questions.explanation: Koldihwa is an important archaeological site belonging to the Neolithic and Chalcolithic periods, located in the present-day state of Uttar Pradesh, India.

questions.question: Mahagara is in present day
questions.explanation: Mahagara is an important Neolithic archaeological site located in the Prayagraj district of Uttar Pradesh, India, near the Belan River valley.

questions.question: Gufkral is in present day
questions.explanation: Gufkral is an important Neolithic archaeological site located in the Tral area of the Pulwama district in Jammu and Kashmir, India.

questions.question: Burzahom is in present day
questions.explanation: Burzahom is a prominent Neolithic archaeological site located in the Srinagar district of Jammu and Kashmir, India, known for its unique pit dwellings.

questions.question: Chirand is in present day
questions.explanation: Chirand is an important Neolithic archaeological site located in the Saran district of Bihar, India, situated on the banks of the Ghaghra River.

questions.question: Hallur is in present day
questions.explanation: Hallur is an important Neolithic and Iron Age archaeological site located in the Haveri district of Karnataka, India.

questions.question: Paiyampalli is in present day
questions.explanation: Paiyampalli is an important Neolithic and Iron Age archaeological site located in the Tirupattur district (formerly part of Vellore district) of Tamil Nadu, India.

questions.question: In early times, groups of herders and farmers living together were called
questions.explanation: In early times, people lived in groups such as tribes, which typically consisted of families and communities sharing common customs, occupations like farming and herding, and living in villages.

questions.question: Daojali Hading is in present day
questions.explanation: Daojali Hading is an important Neolithic site located in the Dima Hasao district (formerly North Cachar Hills) of Assam, India, known for its polished stone tools and jadeite.

questions.question: The place Çatalhöyük was found in which country?
questions.explanation: Çatalhöyük is a very large Neolithic and Chalcolithic settlement located in southern Anatolia in present-day Turkey.

questions.question: What things were found in Çatalhöyük?
options: Flint from Syria, shells from the Red Sea, and cowries from the Mediterranean
Bronze statues and written clay tablets
questions.explanation: At Çatalhöyük, archaeologists found many items that were brought from other places, such as flint from Syria, cowries from the Red Sea, and shells from the Mediterranean, showing early long-distance trade.
